 No stopping Aaron-Roy King in Japan Masters
 No stopping Aaron-Roy King in Japan Masters
 14-Nov-2026, 15:58 14 Nov 2026, 15:58 K. Parkaran Share The newly paired Malaysian men's doubles duo will be making their second final appearance in a major tournament in five weeks.
 Aaron Tai-Yap Roy King, who won the Arctic Open, are hoping to add a second title to their resume when they face Takuro Hoki-Yugo Kobayashi in the Japan Masters final tomorrow. 
 PETALING JAYA : Malaysian men’s doubles pair Aaron Tai-Yap Roy King continued their impressive run today by defeating Denmark’s Daniel Lundgaard-Mads Vestergaard to reach the Japan Masters final. 
 The Malaysians, ranked world No 57, beat the world No 13 Danish pair 21-18, 21-18 in 38 minutes in the semi-finals at the Kumamoto Prefectural Gymnasium.
 Aaron, 20, and Roy King, 25, have maintained their impressive form in the tournament, winning all four of their matches in straight games.
 They will face Japan’s Takuro Hoki-Yugo Kobayashi in tomorrow’s final, following the Japanese pair’s victory over China’s Wang Chang-Xie Haonan in the other semi-final.
 The final will be the Malaysians’ second since joining forces last month.
 They won the Arctic Open title in their debut tournament together before reaching the semi-finals of the Hylo Open in Germany three weeks later.
 Among the pairs they have beaten on their way to the final are world No 5 compatriots Goh Sze Fei-Nur Izzuddin Rumsani, Chinese Taipei’s world No 15 pair Lee Jhe-Huei-Yang Po-Hsuan, and Japan’s world No 16 pair Kakeru Kumagai-Hiroki Nishi.
